extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, supervisory patent examiners, and patent prosecution practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural guidance for patent examiners on searching, considering submissions (including replies to 37 CFR 1.105 requirements and IDSs), preparing/using Patentability Reports, and making rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101/102/103. Emphasizes uniform application of patentability standards and proper recordation of examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of areas of search for 37 CFR 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: Information constituting identification of areas of search must be considered and the examiner must indicate which areas were used and which areas were not used in performing a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indication may be placed in the file wrapper search notes, or by notations on the applicant’s reply with the examiner’s initials and date, and with a notation in the file wrapper search notes that searching based on the 37 CFR 1.105 requirement was made according to the notes on the applicant’s reply. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of answers to examiner queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Information constituting answers to queries posed by the examiner or another Office employee must be considered, and the record must indicate that the answers were considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indication may be made minimally by indicating 'Considered' with the initials and date of the person making such consideration on the reply. For IFW processing, see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of art submitted in response to 37 CFR 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: Art submitted in response to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement must be considered, at least to the extent that art submitted with an Information Disclosure Statement under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant provides a written list of citations with a reply, the examiner must indicate on that list which art has been considered and which has not, in the same manner as with an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98. If the applicant provides no such list, the examiner need not prepare such a list or otherwise make the submitted art of record unless the examiner relies on such art in a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation for 37 CFR 1.105 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information beyond the scope of a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement, submitted along with responsive information, need not be considered unless that submission conforms to 37 CFR 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 609.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criteria for measuring the scope of a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement is the plain meaning of the text of the requirement, so the scope must be carefully specified. If art beyond the scope is submitted in accordance with 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 609, it must be considered according to those provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 are not replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking withdrawal/modification of a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement or to have information considered may submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.181, but a petition is not a reply to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period for reply to the 1.105 requirement continues to run even if a petition has been submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of initial replies to IDS requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial reply responsive to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement and submitted within the original reply period does not have to satisfy the fee and/or certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should list the references on a copy of Form PTO/SB/08 to have the citations entered in the record. Any replies subsequent to the initial reply must meet the provisions of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 as appropriate. Submission of art beyond the scope of 1.105 is treated as a submission under 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 609 and must meet those provisions to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final reliance on art submitted under 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: Where information is submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of the application of such art are necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes practice following a 1.105 reply from practice after an IDS under 1.97/1.98 (see MPEP § 609.04(b) and § 706.07(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use Patentability Reports (P.R.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application assigned to one Technology Center contains claims classifiable in other TCs that are not divisible inter se, the application may be referred to the other TC(s) for a Patentability Report signed by the primary examiner in the reporting TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The P.R. is a memorandum including citations of pertinent references and a complete action on the claims involved. The field of search covered should be endorsed on the file wrapper. Use of P.R. practice is limited to extraordinary circumstances (see MPEP § 705.01(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and request procedure for P.R.
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patentability Report is prepared when primary examiners from both the requesting and requested TCs agree and the requesting TC Director approves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward the application with a memorandum (e.g., 'For Patentability Report from TC -- as to claims --'). For IFW processing see IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and disposition of P.R.
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner in the reporting TC directs preparation of the P.R., which will include citation of all pertinent references and a complete action on all claims involved; when signed it will be returned to the TC of regular assignment and placed in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the primary examiner of the TC of jurisdiction agrees with the P.R., incorporate its substance in the action. If the primary examiner does not agree, they may make their own action and remove the P.R. from the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling disagreements on P.R. findings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner in the jurisdictional TC does not agree with the P.R., they may consult with the reporting examiner; if agreement cannot be reached, the jurisdictional examiner need not rely on the P.R. and may make their own action, removing the P.R. from the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the jurisdictional examiner agrees, incorporate the P.R. substance; the P.R. remains in the file until final disposition (allowance/abandonment) and should then be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer/appeal practice with P.R.
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is taken from rejection of claims all examinable in the reporting TC and the application is otherwise allowable, formal transfer to that TC should be made for appeal purposes; the receiving TC takes jurisdiction and prepares the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At allowance, the application may issue from that TC with classification determined by the controlling claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of examination when P.R. disputes arise
rubrics_metrics.description: If supervisory examiners cannot agree as to order of examination by their TCs, the supervisory examiner having jurisdiction will direct that a complete search be made of the art relevant to their claims prior to referring the application for a P.R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TC to which the application is referred will be advised of the results of this search; if different sequence is expedient, modify the order accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and recording Patentability Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Forwarding an application for a P.R. is not treated as a transfer by the forwarding TC; when completed and returned, it is not counted as a receipt or action by transfer though credit is given for time spent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date status in the reporting TC is determined on the basis of dates in the TC of original jurisdiction; timely reminders should be furnished to the TC making the P.R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate prints of drawings for P.R. purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: In P.R. applications with drawings, the examiner assigned will furnish prints of applicable drawing sheets to the reporting TC for interference search purposes and may indicate this by pencil notation on the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an application that had P.R. prosecution is passed for issue or abandoned, notify each TC that submitted a P.R. at once; the reporting TC will note the date of allowance/abandonment on the duplicate prints, which may be destroyed when of no value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on use of Patentability Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: P.R. practice is not obligatory and should be used only where it will save total examiner time or improve quality due to specialized knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where claims are directed to the same character of invention but differ in scope only, prosecution by P.R. is never proper. Exemplary situations ordinarily not proper for P.R. include: (A) claims related as manufacturing process and product defined by the process; (B) claims related as product and a process that merely makes the product; (C) claims related as a combination distinguished only by characteristics of a subcombination and that subcombination per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews involving P.R.
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where an interview is held on an application with a P.R., the reporting TC may be called on for assistance at the interview when it concerns claims treated by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 713–713.10 regarding interviews in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and goal of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the application and understanding the claimed invention, a prior art search is made and the application is reviewed with the prior art to determine whether the claims define a useful, novel, nonobvious, and enabled invention clearly described in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal of examination is to clearly articulate any rejection early in prosecution so the applicant can provide evidence of patentability and reply completely at the earliest opportunity. Examiner then reviews all evidence before issuing next Office action. If information reasonably necessary should be required from the applicant under 37 CFR 1.105, that requirement should generally be made prior to or with the first Office action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection language and citation of references
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, the claims or those considered unpatentable will be rejected. In rejecting claims for want of novelty or obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reference is complex or shows inventions other than that claimed, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable. The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and facts known to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination) as to any matter affecting patentability and may rely upon facts within his or her knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions in the specification or made during prosecution may be used for anticipation or obviousness determinations regardless of statutory category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subject matter developed by another under 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To overcome a 103 rejection based on such subject matter via 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2), the applicant must provide a statement that the prior art and the claimed invention were made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the date of invention, that the claimed invention was made as a result of activities within the scope of that agreement, and that the application discloses the names of the parties to the joint research agreement. Definitions of 'joint research agreement' are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of patentability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of patentability (novelty, usefulness, unobviousness, enablement) must be the same throughout the Office in every art, regardless of whether the art is complex, newly developed, crowded, or competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application should not be allowed unless issues pertinent to patentability have been raised and resolved in examination and prosecution. Apply the 'preponderance of the evidence' test: reject a claim if, in view of prior art and evidence of record, it is more likely than not unpatentable. Recitation of detailed features ('picture' claim) is not itself justification for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling defects in form or omission of a limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: When patentable subject matter is disclosed but claims cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection/rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s action should be constructive and when possible should offer a definite suggestion for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting patentable subject matter disclosed but not claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner is satisfied that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and record indicates applicant intends to claim it, the examiner may note in the Office action that certain aspects/features of the invention have not been claimed and that if properly claimed such claims may be given favorable consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This serves to inform applicant of unclaimed patentable matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after applicant reply (37 CFR 1.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reply by applicant to a non-final action, the application will be reconsidered and again examined; the applicant will be notified if claims are rejected, objections/requirements made, or decisions favorable to patentability made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may reply to such Office action in the same manner provided in 37 CFR 1.111 (or §1.945 for reexamination) unless the Office action indicates it is final, an appeal has been taken, or it closes prosecution in certain reexamination contexts. Amendments after an appeal are subject to 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between rejections and objections
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'rejection' is refusal to grant claims because subject matter is unpatentable (merits); an 'objection' addresses form (e.g., dependency on a rejected claim if dependent claim otherwise allowable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term 'rejected' for claims denied on merits. A rejection is subject to review by the Board; objections and formal matters are not decided by the Board and should not be combined in appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art rejections should use the best available art
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art rejections ordinarily should be confined strictly to the best available art; the language used should be unequivocal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allowed where propriety turns on claim interpretation, a claim is met only in terms by a reference not disclosing inventive concept, or a pertinent reference may be antedated by affidavit/declaration. Such rejections should be backed up by the best other art available and avoid merely cumulative rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on abstracts and foreign-language documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When an abstract or foreign-language document is uncovered in search and both the abstract and underlying document qualify as prior art, a copy of the underlying document must be obtained and analyzed; if not in English, a translation must be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record must be clear whether the examiner relies on the abstract or the full text document. Abstract-only reliance is generally inappropriate where both are prior art. In limited circumstances an examiner may rely on an abstract in a non-final action and supply full text/translation in the next Office action; whether the next action may be final is governed by MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admitted prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement by an applicant in the specification or made during prosecution identifying the work of another as 'prior art' is an admission which can be relied upon for anticipation and obviousness determinations regardless of statutory categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the admitted prior art anticipates the claim but does not qualify as prior art under any paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 102, the claim may be rejected as anticipated by the admitted prior art without citing to 35 U.S.C. 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation) and 103 (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102, the reference must teach every aspect of the claimed invention explicitly or implicitly; any feature not directly taught must be inherently present. For 35 U.S.C. 103, the reference teachings must be modified to meet the claims and the modification must have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the distinction in mind when framing rejections; see MPEP §§ 2131–2146 for further guidance on patentability determinations under 102 and 103.
